items.subtype_name: Largest population the results apply to
items.stimulus:
Astronomers randomly selected 200 stars from a catalog of all stars within 50 light-years of the Sun. The selected stars that have at least one confirmed planet are summarized below.

Selected Stars With at Least One Confirmed Planet
Star type | Number of stars | Average number of planets
Red dwarf | 18 | 2
Sun-like | 9 | 3
Other | 3 | 1
items.stem: Which of the following is the largest population to which the results shown in the table can be generalized?
choices: The 30 selected stars that have at least one confirmed planet
All stars within 50 light-years of the Sun that have at least one confirmed planet
All stars within 50 light-years of the Sun, with or without a confirmed planet
All stars in the Milky Way galaxy that have at least one confirmed planet
items.explanation: The 200 stars were randomly selected from stars within 50 light-years of the Sun, but the table shows only those with at least one confirmed planet. The table's results therefore reach stars within 50 light-years of the Sun that also have at least one confirmed planet. You keep both the distance limit and the planet condition.

A.why: You named the stars in the table instead of the population they represent. These stars came from a random sample, so they speak for the matching stars in the whole catalog.

C.why: You dropped the condition that defines the table. It includes only stars with at least one confirmed planet, so its averages can't describe stars that have none.

D.why: You widened the region from 50 light-years to the whole galaxy. Only nearby stars could be selected, so the sample can't speak for distant ones.

items.subtype_name: Largest population the results apply to
items.stimulus:
A labor economist randomly selected 200 workers from all warehouse workers employed by Brightline Logistics at its Ohio sites. Each selected worker reported their weekly hours and hourly wage. The table shows the results only for the selected workers who work at least 30 hours per week.

Workers Working at Least 30 Hours per Week
Weekly hours | Number of workers | Mean hourly wage
30 to 39 | 64 | $19
40 or more | 92 | $21
items.stem: Which of the following is the largest population to which the results in the table can be generalized?
choices: Only the 156 sampled workers who work at least 30 hours per week
All warehouse workers employed by Brightline Logistics in Ohio
Brightline's Ohio warehouse workers who work at least 30 hours per week
All Ohio warehouse workers who work at least 30 hours per week
items.explanation: The 200 workers were chosen at random from Brightline's Ohio warehouse workers. The table, however, shows only the workers who work at least 30 hours per week. So the results in the table apply to Brightline's Ohio warehouse workers who meet that 30-hour threshold.

A.why: You chose the sampled workers themselves instead of the population. Because the workers were randomly selected, the results can extend beyond them.

B.why: You dropped the 30-hour threshold. The table leaves out workers with fewer hours, so its results say nothing about them.

D.why: You widened the group from one company to every warehouse in Ohio. Only Brightline's workers could have been selected.
